rule_name: General Matter Approval Voting Thresholds
rule_statement_normalized: A General Matter requires approval by vote of the Parties. If there are only two Parties, mutual consent is required, but a Party with at least 66% voting interest may unilaterally approve. If there are three or more Parties, approval requires affirmative vote of two or more Parties holding combined voting interest of at least 51%, but a Party with at least 66% voting interest may unilaterally approve, except for certain Operations.

a) should there be only two (2) Parties to this Agreement a General Matter approval shall require mutual consent of the Parties; provided, however, a Party having a voting interest of at least sixty-six percent (66%) may unilaterally approve such General Matter.
b) should there be three (3) or more Parties to this Agreement, a General Matter approval shall require the affirmative vote of two (2) or more of the Parties having a combined voting interest of fifty-one percent (51%) or more; provided, however, a Party having a voting interest of at least sixty-six percent (66%) may unilaterally approve such General Matter. except as to any Of'the following proposed Operations: (i) Exploratory Operations (Article 10); (ii) Appraisal Operations (Article 11); or (Hi) Development Operations (Article 13). In this event such Operation will require an Election by the Parties rather than requiring the prior approval by the Parties as a General Matter.

Failure to respond in a timely manner shall be deemed an vote not to participate. rule_name: Participation Election for Proposed Operations
rule_statement_normalized: Parties must make a participation Election for any proposed Operation where failure to approve and participate invokes non-consent, acreage forfeiture, or underinvestment provisions. Each Party must notify the Operator and other Parties of its Election. Participation Election for Exploratory or Appraisal expendable wells includes all necessary expenditures for drilling to Objective Depth, testing (except production testing), logging, and plugging as set out in the AFE and Well Plan. Participation Election for Appraisal or Development Wells not drilled as expendable wells includes all necessary expenditures through abandonment or temporary abandonment.
source_quote: The Parties shall make a participation Election (and without necessity for any vote) for any proposed Operation where failure to approve and participate in the operation invokes the terms of any non-consent provision, acreage forfeiture provision or underinvestment in this Agreement. source_quote: Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement, all notices and responses required or permitted by this Agreement will be in writing and will be delivered in person or by mail, courier service, or facsimile transmission, with postage and charges prepaid, addressed to the Parties at the addresses in Exhibit "A" (Working Interest of the Parties, Operator and Representatives of the Parties). rule_name: Removal of Operator for Cause by Vote
rule_statement_normalized: The Operator may be removed for cause by vote of the Parties as a General Matter if the Operator commits any of the following acts: insolvency or inability to pay debts as they mature; appointment of a receiver for the Operator or substantially all of its property; gross negligence or willful misconduct; inability to meet operational standards in Articles 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, and 5.6; substantial breach of a material provision of the Agreement not cured within 30 days after notice, or longer if corrective action is begun within 30 days and diligently pursued.

(e) the Operator commits a substantial breach of a material provision of this Agreement and fails to cure same within thirty (30) days after receipt of notice of such breach. However, if the breach specified in the notice is of such a nature that it reasonably cannot be corrected within the thirty (30) day period, and the Operator within said period begins corrective action or steps to correct the breach and thereafter diligently carries such corrective action to completion, the Operator shall not be removed. Effective Date of Resignation or Removal: The resignation or removal of the Operator shall become effective at 7:00 a.m. on the first day of the month following a period of ninety (90) days after said notice, unless a longer period of time is required to obtain approval by the Minerals Management Service.

rule_name: Non-Consent Operation Recoupment and Reversion
rule_statement_normalized: Each Participating Party holds interest, rights, and title to future Hydrocarbon production in proportion to their Working Interest during the Non-Consent Operation or Hydrocarbon production. Upon Participating Parties recouping from the Non-Participating Party's Share of future Hydrocarbon production an amount equal to the Costs of the Non-Consent Operation multiplied by the applicable recoupment percentage, the Working Interest, leasehold operating rights, and title to future Hydrocarbon production revert to the former Non-Participating Party, who then becomes a Participating Party in the Non-Consent Operation.
source_quote: Such interest, rights. and title to future Hydrocarbon production shall revert to each Non-Participating Party when the Participating Party has recouped from the Non-Participating Party's Share of proceeds of future Hydrocarbon production from such Non-Consent Operation an amount equal to the product of the Costs of the Non-Consent Operation multiplied by the recoupment percentage for each operation set out below. The Non-Participating Party's Share of the Non-Consent Operation shall be reduced (to the extent of the Non-Participating Party's prior Working Interest) by any third-party cash contribution credited to the Non-Consent Operation. Upon recoupment by the Participating Parties of the recoupment percentage, the Working Interest and leasehold operating rights in the Non-Consent Operation, along with the title to any future Hydrocarbon Production therefrom, shall revert to the former Non-Participating Party and the former Non-Participating Party shall become a Participating Party in the Non-Consent Operation.

rule_name: Recoupment from Hydrocarbon Production for Non-Consent Operations Resulting in Discovery
rule_statement_normalized: Recoupment for a Non-Consent Operation resulting in discovery or extension of a Producible Reservoir shall be made from the Non-Participating Party's Share of Hydrocarbon production as follows: (i) 100% of the Non-Participating Party's Share of production from the Non-Consent Operation well if completed for production, and 50% of the Non-Participating Party's Share of production from all wells subsequently drilled and completed in the discovered or extended Producible Reservoir; (ii) 50% of the Non-Participating Party's Share of production from all wells drilled from and/or produced through the Subsequent Production System or Facilities and/or wells benefited from injection or disposal wells. Interest reverts to Non-Participating Party only after Participating Parties have fully recouped specified amounts.

source_quote: Recoupment for a Non-Consent Operation which results in a discovery of a Producible Reservoir or extension of an existing Producible Reservoir shall be made from the following portions of the Non-Participating Party's Share of Hydrocarbon production: (i) Subsequent Exploratory Operations. Appraisal Wells, or Development Wells: Recoupment shall be taken from one hundred percent (100%) of the Non-Participating Party's Share of all Hydrocarbon production from the Non-Consent Operation (if the well is completed for Hydrocarbon production), and from fifty percent (50%) of the Non-Participating Party's Share of Hydrocarbon production from all wells subsequently drilled and completed in the Producible Reservoir discovered by said Non-Consent Operations or the extended portion of an existing Producible Reservoir discovered by said Non-Consent Operation and in which the Non-Participating Party has a Participating Interest. (ii) Non-consent Subsequent Production Systems and Facilities: Recoupment shall be taken from fifty percent (50%) of the Non-Participating Party's share of Hydrocarbon production from all wells which are drilled from and/or produced through the Subsequent Production System or Facilities and/or wells benefited from injection or disposal wells. The interest shall revert to each Non-Participating Party only after the Participating Parties have completely recouped, from Hydrocarbon production, the amounts specified herein.

rule_name: Makeup Gas Allocation by Fractional Ownership
rule_statement_normalized: The Underproduced Party shall be entitled to take monthly an additional percentage of the Overproduced Party's Fractional Ownership of each Pricing Category of Gas: 10% from November 1 to March 31, and 50% from April 1 to October 31, unless otherwise agreed. The Underproduced Party's share of Makeup Gas shall not exceed 50% of the Overproduced Party's Fractional Ownership of Gas unless otherwise agreed. If multiple Underproduced or Overproduced Parties exist, each party's share of Makeup Gas shall be proportional to its Fractional Ownership relative to the total Fractional Ownership of all Underproduced or Overproduced Parties respectively.
source_quote: the Underproduced Party for a Pricing Category shall be entitled to take monthly: (1) for the calendar period beginning November 1 and ending March 31, an additional ten percent (10%) of the Overproduced Party's Fractional Ownership of each Pricing Category of Gas; and (2) for the period beginning April 1 and ending October 31, an additional fifty percent (50%), of the Overproduced Party's Fractional Ownership of each Pricing Category of Gas, unless otherwise agreed to by the Parties. In no event will the Underproduced Party's share of Makeup Gas be allowed to exceed fifty percent (50%) of the Overproduced party's Fractional Ownership of Gas unless otherwise agreed to by the Parties. Subject to the Makeup limitations specified above, in the event that there is more than one Underproduced Party and Overproduced Party, unless otherwise agreed, each Underproduced Party and Overproduced Party's share of Makeup Gas shall be the direct proportion of its Fractional Ownership to the total Fractional Ownership of all Underproduced or Overproduced Parties, respectively taking or furnishing Makeup Gas.

rule_name: Operator Mortgage Limit
rule_statement_normalized: The Operator's liability under the Agreement and the mortgage and security interest granted to Non-Operating Parties is limited to the actual obligations and indebtedness outstanding and unpaid attributable to the Operator's interest, and shall not exceed $25,000,000 in aggregate.

Such interest, rights and title to future Hydrocarbon production shall revert to each Non-Participating Party when the Participating Party has recouped from the Non-Participating Party's Share of proceeds of future Hydrocarbon production from such Non-Consent Operation an amount equal to the product of the Participating Party's share of the Costs of the Non-Consent Operation multiplied by the recoupment percentage for each Operation set out below. rule_name: Over-Investment and Recoupment in Deepening Operation
rule_statement_normalized: If a Non-Participating Party elects to participate in the Deepening Operation, the Participating Parties shall be deemed over-invested to the extent of the Non-Participating Party's Share of Costs in the original Non-Consent Operation (less any amount recovered by the Participating Parties out of the Non-Participating Party's Share of Hydrocarbon production or through a Disproportionate Spending Settlement). If the Participating Parties have recouped the Cost of the well at the time they desire to Deepen the well, then the Non-Participating Party will not be under-invested in the Deepening. However, the Participating Parties in the original well shall still be permitted complete recoupment from other wells in the Producible Reservoir discovered or extended by the original well until the total non-consent amount to be recouped has been recovered.

rule_statement_normalized: Permitted Over-expenditure means an amount equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the original approved AFE or a specified dollar amount, whichever is less, varying by AFE type: $3,000,000 for Wells and Subsequent Operations, $3,000,000 for Project Team AFE, $6,000,000 for Final Design AFE, $10,000,000 for Fabrication AFE, and $3,000,000 for all other AFEs.
source_quote:
In relation to the drilling of Exploratory Wells, Appraisal Wells or Development Wells, or Subsequent Appraisal Operations or Subsequent Development Operations or Subsequent Exploratory Operations, the Permitted Over-expenditure means an amount equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the original approved AFE for such well or operation or three million dollars ($3,000,000.00), whichever is less.

In relation to the Project Team, the Permitted Over-expenditure means an amount equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the original approved Project Team AFE or three million dollars ($3,000,000.00), whichever is less.

In relation to the Final Design AFE, the Permitted Over-expenditure means an amount equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the original approved Final Design AFE or six million dollars ($6,000,000.00), whichever is less.

In relation to the Fabrication AFE, the Permitted Over-expenditure means an amount equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the original approved Fabrication AFE or ten million dollars ($10,000,000.00), whichever is less.

In relation to all other Cost overruns, the Permitted Over-expenditure means an amount equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the original approved AFE for such activity or operation or three million dollars ($3,000,000.00), whichever is less.

rule_statement_normalized: In an irreconcilable conflict between Section 1 of the agreement and the Direct Charges section of the Applicable Accounting Procedure, Section 1 terms control to the limited extent of the conflict.
source_quote: in the event of an irreconcilable conflict between the terms of Section 1 of this Agreement and the terms of Section II (Direct Charges) of the Applicable Accounting Procedure, the terms of Section 1 of this Agreement shall control to the limited extent of the irreconcilable conflict.
scope_in: Direct charge cost categories
conditions: Only in irreconcilable conflict, limited to extent of conflict

rule_name: Section 1 Applies Where Accounting Procedure Silent
rule_statement_normalized: Where the Applicable Accounting Procedure omits or is silent on any cost category stated in Section 1, the Section 1 terms apply and are deemed consistent with the Accounting Procedure.
source_quote: to the extent that the Applicable Accounting Procedure omits or is silent as to any cost or category of costs stated in Section 1 of this Agreement, the terms of Section 1 will apply and such application is deemed consistent with the Applicable Accounting Procedure.
scope_in: Costs stated in Section 1
conditions: Accounting Procedure silent or omits the cost category

rule_name: OTL Rules Subject to Accounting Procedure
rule_statement_normalized: Charges under the Agreed OTL Definition and Rules remain subject to all other provisions of the Applicable Accounting Procedure.
source_quote: charges described in Section II, shall be subject to all other provisions of the Applicable Accounting Procedure.
scope_in: OTL charges
conditions: Subject to other Accounting Procedure provisions

rule_name: Affiliate OTL Chargeability
rule_statement_normalized: OTL can occur when the Operator uses an affiliate; in such cases the same OTL chargeability standards established in the agreement apply.
source_quote: It is also acknowledged that OTL can occur when the Operator has chosen to utilize an affiliate; in such cases, the same OTL chargeability standards established in this Agreement apply.
scope_in: Affiliate-performed offsite technical labor
conditions: OTL performed by an affiliate of the Operator

rule_name: Regulatory-Mandated OTL
rule_statement_normalized: OTL activities required to comply with BSEE and applicable law/regulation, including the mandatory SEMS program under 30 CFR 250.1902, are covered as mandatory OTL regulatory requirements for drilling, completion and well intervention.
source_quote: Environmental Enforcement (BSEE), and any applicable law or regulation, including but not limited to the activities included in the required SEMS program pursuant to 30 CFR 250.1902...Mandatory OTL regulatory requirements for drilling, completion, and well intervention
scope_in: Regulatory OTL for drilling, completion, well intervention
conditions: Activity mandated by BSEE / applicable law / SEMS program

rule_name: OTL Definition Resolution
rule_statement_normalized: The Parties agreed to resolve and settle the definition of Offsite Technical Labor (OTL) and the historic and future joint account charges associated with OTL.
source_quote: resolve (i) certain disagreements and misalignments relating to the definition of Offsite Technical Labor ("OTL") and historic and future joint account charges associated with OTL
conditions: Charges to the joint account associated with OTL are governed by the settled OTL definition.

rule_name: Remote Technology Center Definition
rule_statement_normalized: A Remote Technology Center is any facility, regardless of location, having dedicated technical and/or operations staffing that directly monitors and/or controls Joint Operations on a real-time basis.
source_quote: "Remote Technology Center" shall mean a facility, regardless of location, having dedicated technical and/or operations staffing, that directly monitors and/or controls Joint Operations on a real-time basis
conditions: Facility must have dedicated technical/operations staffing directly monitoring or controlling Joint Operations in real time; includes listed BP and SOI facilities and successors.

rule_name: Applicable Accounting Procedures Governance
rule_statement_normalized: Accounting procedures utilized by the parties are those contained in the applicable Exhibit to each Applicable Operating Agreement, including any agreed Statement of Clarification and Intent addendum.
source_quote: "Applicable Accounting Procedures" shall mean the accounting procedures contained in the applicable Exhibit to each of the Applicable Operating Agreements setting forth the accounting procedures to be utilized by the parties thereto
conditions: Applies as set forth in each Applicable Operating Agreement's accounting procedure exhibit and any agreed addendum.

rule_name: Phase II / II(a) Audit Exceptions Netting and Settlement
rule_statement_normalized: Phase II and Phase II(a) Audit Exceptions are netted so only the excess amount of $668,543 is due, payable by BP to Shell via electronic transfer.
source_quote: Phase II Audit Exceptions and Phase II(a) Audit Exceptions will be netted so that only the excess amount shall be due, being six hundred sixty eight thousand five hundred forty three Dollars ($668,543)
conditions: Payment made simultaneously with transfer of amounts owed under the 2017 Settlement Agreement.

rule_name: Waiver of Audit Exception Claims Except Materials
rule_statement_normalized: Each Party waives and releases all claims relating to the Phase II and Phase II(a) Audit Exceptions, with the sole exception of claims for Materials set forth in Exhibit A, which remain pending.
source_quote: Each Party waives, releases and will hold harmiess the other Party from any and all claiins... relating to the Phase II Audit Exceptions and Phase II(a) Audit Exceptions, with the sole exception of claims for Materials set forth in Exhibit A
conditions: Material claims listed in Exhibit A are not resolved and remain pending; all other audit exception claims are waived.

rule_name: Billing Standards Effective Date
rule_statement_normalized: The billing standards in Section 3 apply to charges submitted by a Party acting as Operator under the Applicable Operating Agreements commencing January 1, 2014.
source_quote: the standards articulated in this Section 3 below shall apply to charges submitted by a Party, when acting as an Operator under the Applicable Operating Agreements, commencing January 1, 2014
conditions: Applies to charges by a Party acting as Operator from January 1, 2014 onward.

rule_name: Operational Manual Updates Direct Charge
rule_statement_normalized: Each Party may charge the Joint Account as a direct charge for costs of operational manual development and updates specific to the Joint Operations, regardless of location, but only to the extent such manuals will be used in the Joint Operations.
source_quote: Each Party is permitted to charge the Joint Account as a direct charge for the costs incurred for operational manual development and updates (Site Operating Procedures, etc.) that are specific to the Joint Operations, regardless of the location of the work
conditions: Manuals/updates must be specific to Joint Operations and only to the extent they will be used in the Joint Operations.

rule_name: Accumulator Account Rig-Related Cost Capture
rule_statement_normalized: The Accumulator Account is used to capture and allocate various rig-related costs associated with US Gulf of Mexico activity sets, including acquiring/assuring a rig, rig modifications during the contract term, additional support costs incurred by the contracting company, and mobilization/demobilization costs.
source_quote: "Accumulator Account" shall mean the account used to capture and allocate the various rig-related costs associated with US Gulf of Mexico activity sets on (i) acquiring and assuring a rig, (i) rig modifications made during the term of a rig contract, (iii) additional costs that the contracting company incurs in assistance and support of rig operations, and (iv) costs associated with mobilization and demobilization of the rig.
conditions: Costs must be rig-related and associated with US Gulf of Mexico activity sets across the four enumerated categories

rule_name: Initial Mobilization Costs Originating Outside GOM
rule_statement_normalized: Any rig-related costs associated with initial mobilization, which may originate outside the US Gulf of Mexico, may be included in the Accumulator Account.
source_quote: Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, any rig related costs associated with initial mobilization, which may originate outside the US Gulf of Mexico, may be included in the Accumulator Account.
conditions: Costs must be associated with initial mobilization even if originating outside the US Gulf of Mexico

rule_name: Additional Accumulator Account Cost Categories
rule_statement_normalized: The Accumulator Account may also capture costs related to construction oversight, fuel, rig commissioning, inspections, rig modifications (tangible and intangible), costs directly associated with mobilization, load out, suspended operations, major maintenance, rig repairs, program moves to a new area of operation, and demobilization costs.
source_quote: Without limitation to the foregoing, the account may also capture costs related to construction oversight, fuel, rig commissioning, inspections, rig modifications (both tangible and intangible), costs directly associated with mobilization, load out, suspended operations (i.e., acts of god, acts of government, regulatory order/requirement or force majeure), major maintenance, rig repairs, program moves to a new area of operation, and demobilization costs.
conditions: Suspended operations limited to acts of god, acts of government, regulatory order/requirement or force majeure

rule_name: Accumulator Account Amortization and Allocation
rule_statement_normalized: The aggregated costs in the Accumulator Account are amortized over the remaining term of the rig contract and allocated based on rig usage.
source_quote: The aggregated costs in the account are then amortized over the remaining term of the rig contract and ailocated based on rig usage.
conditions: Allocation based on rig usage; amortized over remaining term of rig contract

rule_name: Demobilization and True-up Charge Chargeability (Disputed)
rule_statement_normalized: The Parties were misaligned as to whether a Party, acting as operator, can charge the other Party its proportionate share of certain demobilization and true-up charges described in Exhibit A.
source_quote: "Demobilization and True-up Charge Disputes" shall mean misalignment between the Parties as to whether a Party, acting in its capacity as the operator, can charge the other Party its proportionate share of those certain demobilization and true-up charge disputes described in Exhibit A, attached hereto and incorporated herein.
conditions: Chargeability of proportionate share subject to dispute resolution; charging Party must act in capacity as operator; charges as described in Exhibit A

rule_name: Affiliate Contractors' Overlay Charge Under GW UOA
rule_statement_normalized: The permissible Affiliate contractors' overlay charge under the GW UOA is governed by the terms documented in the Amendment to Great White Alaminos Canyon Block 857 Unit Operating Agreement, effective as of January 1, 2013.
source_quote: the Parties shall execute the Amendment to Great White Alaminos Canyon Block 857 Unit Operating Agreement, attached hereto and incorporated herein as Exhibit "B", which documents the Parties' agreement on the permissible Affiliate contractors' overlay charge under the GW UOA effective as of January 1, 2013.
conditions: Permissible only as documented/limited by the Amendment (Exhibit B) to the GW UOA; effective as of January 1, 2013. The specific overlay charge amount/percentage is defined in Exhibit B (not included in this text).
